drivingQuestion: Which tanna holds that where the seller retains a residue of wool, the obligation follows the seller?
outcomeNote: The unit consists of the question alone; the identification of the tanna is not given within these segments.

segments.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ גֵּז צֹאנוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ כּוּ׳. מַאן תַּנָּא דְּהֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא שִׁיּוּרָא גַּבֵּי מוֹכֵר, בָּתַר מוֹכֵר אָזְלִינַן?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to «one who purchases the fleece of the sheep of another» Jew, if the seller kept some of the wool, then he is obligated to give the first sheared wool to the priest. If the seller did not keep any of the wool, the buyer is obligated to give it. The Gemara asks: «Who» is the tanna who «taught that» in a case «where there is residual» wool «in» the possession of the «seller, we follow the seller» in determining who is obligated in the mitzva of first sheared wool?

moves.summary: The mishna's clause on buying a fellow Jew's fleece is quoted.
moves.about: the mishna's ruling that when the seller kept some wool the seller gives the first sheared wool

moves.cueHe: מאן תנא דהיכא דאיכא שיורא גבי מוכר
moves.summary: Whose view is it that a retained residue makes the seller the one obligated?
moves.about: which tanna holds that where the seller retains a residue we follow the seller rather than the buyer
